deck_name: 君の名は。 Ch.2 端緒 — Core Words
source: 新海誠『君の名は。』(角川つばさ文庫), 第二章「端緒」
notes: Everyday words for Chapter 2: mostly N4–N3, plus a few common N2 words. These are the words the main Vocabulary deck skipped as 'too easy'. They come from the chapter's scenes (waking up in the wrong body, school, Tokyo trains and streets, the café, the restaurant job and the needle, the clues on the phone), not copied page by page. Study this deck before the hard Vocabulary deck. Example sentences are original.

priority_guide.high: Learn before or while reading this chapter — it carries the scene.
priority_guide.medium: Useful; context usually helps if you forget it.
priority_guide.low: Recognition is enough — look it up once, don't over-drill.

difficulty_guide.two_above: N1 / literary — ambitious; learn to recognise it.

kanji_difficulty_guide.easy: Kanji are common; readable at N3.
kanji_difficulty_guide.medium: One or more kanji may trip you — drill the reading.
kanji_difficulty_guide.hard: Rare kanji or irregular reading — learn the kana form first.

cards.scene: With no warning at all, 瀧 wakes up in a stranger's body, and 三葉 wakes up in his.
cards.context: いきなり = abruptly, skipping the usual steps: いきなり怒り出す = to suddenly start shouting. 急に = suddenly (a change); 突然 (とつぜん) is a little more formal. The kanji 行き成り is rare.
cards.example_sentence: 歩いていたら、いきなり雨が降り出した。
cards.example_reading: あるいて いたら、 いきなり あめ が ふりだした。
cards.example_meaning: I was walking along when it suddenly started to rain.

cards.scene: 瀧 wakes up on a futon on the floor of 三葉's room, not in his own bed.
cards.context: 布団を敷く (しく) = to lay out the futon; 布団をたたむ = to fold it away. 掛け布団 = the top quilt, 敷き布団 = the mattress. ベッド is the Western-style bed 瀧 is used to.
cards.example_sentence: 朝起きたら、布団をたたんで押し入れにしまう。
cards.example_reading: あさ おきたら、 ふとん を たたんで おしいれ に しまう。
cards.example_meaning: When I get up in the morning, I fold up the futon and put it away in the closet.

cards.scene: The room 瀧 wakes up in is an old-style Japanese room with a tatami floor.
cards.context: Rooms are measured in mats: 六畳 (ろくじょう) = a six-mat room, with the counter read じょう. 和室 (わしつ) = a Japanese-style room. The verb 畳む (たたむ, to fold) uses the same kanji.
cards.example_sentence: 祖父の家には、畳の部屋が三つある。
cards.example_reading: そふ の いえ に は、 たたみ の へや が みっつ ある。
cards.example_meaning: My grandfather's house has three tatami rooms.

cards.scene: 瀧 opens his eyes and nothing around him looks familiar: not the room, not the window, not the body.
cards.context: 見る + 慣れる (to get used to) → 見慣れる = to be used to seeing; 見慣れない = something you aren't used to seeing. 見慣れた景色 = a familiar view. Plainer than the hard deck's 見知らぬ.
cards.example_sentence: 駅を出ると、見慣れない景色が広がっていた。
cards.example_reading: えき を でる と、 みなれない けしき が ひろがって いた。
cards.example_meaning: When I came out of the station, an unfamiliar scene spread out before me.

cards.scene: What on earth is going on? 瀧 keeps asking himself this all through the strange morning.
cards.context: Goes with a question word and adds surprise or frustration: 一体何?, 一体どうして? = what / why on earth? As a noun, 一体 also means 'one body, a whole' (一体になる = to become one).
cards.example_sentence: こんな夜中に、一体誰が電話してきたんだろう。
cards.example_reading: こんな よなか に、 いったい だれ が でんわ して きた ん だろう。
cards.example_meaning: Who on earth could be calling in the middle of the night?

cards.scene: 瀧 decides this must be a dream. It can't be reality.
cards.context: 夢 (dream) vs 現実 (reality). 現実的 = realistic; 非現実的 = unrealistic; 現実に戻る = to come back to reality.
cards.example_sentence: 夢のような話だが、これは現実だ。
cards.example_reading: ゆめ の ような はなし だ が、 これ は げんじつ だ。
cards.example_meaning: It sounds like a dream, but this is reality.

cards.scene: Is this body real? 瀧 can hardly believe that what he sees and feels is genuine.
cards.context: 本 (true) + 物 (thing). Opposite: 偽物 (にせもの) = a fake. 本物の〜 = a real ~: 本物の革 = real leather.
cards.example_sentence: このかばんは安かったけど、本物の革だそうだ。
cards.example_reading: この かばん は やすかった けど、 ほんもの の かわ だ そう だ。
cards.example_meaning: This bag was cheap, but apparently it's real leather.

cards.scene: 瀧 checks the face in the mirror and the body he's in, to make sure of what he's seeing.
cards.context: 確かめる = to check something with your own eyes or hands. Related: 確か = certain / if I remember right; 確かに = certainly. 確認する (かくにん) is the more formal word.
cards.example_sentence: 家を出る前に、鍵をかけたかもう一度確かめた。
cards.example_reading: いえ を でる まえ に、 かぎ を かけた か もう いちど たしかめた。
cards.example_meaning: Before leaving the house, I checked once more that I'd locked the door.

cards.scene: 瀧 notices an unfamiliar weight on 'his' chest. This is the chapter's most famous comic moment.
cards.context: Both the body part and where feelings sit: 胸が痛む = your heart aches; 胸がどきどきする = your heart pounds. 胸を張る = to puff out your chest with pride.
cards.example_sentence: 発表の前は、緊張で胸がどきどきした。
cards.example_reading: はっぴょう の まえ は、 きんちょう で むね が どきどき した。
cards.example_meaning: Before my presentation, my heart was pounding with nerves.

cards.scene: 瀧 touches his face, his hair, his body. None of it feels like his own.
cards.context: Both 〜に触る and 〜を触る are used. 触れる (ふれる) is softer and more written (a light touch, or touching on a topic). Signs say 触らないでください = please don't touch.
cards.example_sentence: 熱いから、なべに触らないで。
cards.example_reading: あつい から、 なべ に さわらないで。
cards.example_meaning: Don't touch the pot. It's hot.

cards.scene: Both of them panic in someone else's body, and keep rushing to cover their mistakes.
cards.context: 慌てる = to lose your calm and rush. 慌てて = hurriedly, in a panic (慌てて家を出た). 慌てないで = don't panic. 急ぐ just means 'to hurry', with no panic in it.
cards.example_sentence: 電車の時間を間違えて、慌てて駅まで走った。
cards.example_reading: でんしゃ の じかん を まちがえて、 あわてて えき まで はしった。
cards.example_meaning: I got the train time wrong and ran to the station in a panic.

cards.scene: Fits the morning when 四葉 calls her big 'sister' to get up and come down to breakfast.
cards.context: Transitive partner of 起きる: 起きる = I get up; 起こす = I wake someone else up (母に起こされた = I was woken by my mother). Also 'to cause': 事故を起こす = to cause an accident.
cards.example_sentence: 明日は早いから、六時に起こしてくれる?
cards.example_reading: あした は はやい から、 ろくじ に おこして くれる?
cards.example_meaning: I have an early start tomorrow. Can you wake me up at six?

cards.scene: The rushed school morning: at this rate 'Mitsuha' will be late.
cards.context: 遅刻する = to be late for something on a schedule (school, work). 〜に遅れる also works: 授業に遅れる. 寝坊 (oversleeping, Ch.1) is often the reason.
cards.example_sentence: バスが来なくて、学校に遅刻してしまった。
cards.example_reading: バス が こなくて、 がっこう に ちこく して しまった。
cards.example_meaning: The bus didn't come, so I was late for school.

cards.scene: 瀧 has to find his way around a town and a school he has never seen.
cards.context: 道に迷う = to lose your way. It also means 'can't decide': どれにするか迷う = can't decide which one to choose. 迷子 (まいご) = a lost child.
cards.example_sentence: 初めての町で道に迷って、交番で聞いた。
cards.example_reading: はじめて の まち で みち に まよって、 こうばん で きいた。
cards.example_meaning: I got lost in a town I'd never been to, so I asked at the police box.

cards.scene: At school, 瀧 doesn't know which desk is 三葉's.
cards.context: 席に着く (つく) = to take your seat; 席を立つ = to get up from your seat; 席をゆずる = to give up your seat. 座席 (ざせき) = a seat on a train or in a theatre.
cards.example_sentence: 電車でお年寄りに席をゆずった。
cards.example_reading: でんしゃ で おとしより に せき を ゆずった。
cards.example_meaning: I gave up my seat to an elderly person on the train.

cards.scene: 'Mitsuha's' whole manner at school (loud, careless, boyish) baffles her classmates.
cards.context: 態度がいい / 悪い = a good / bad attitude; 態度が大きい = acting big, arrogant; 態度を変える = to change how you act towards someone.
cards.example_sentence: 先生に注意されて、彼は急に態度を変えた。
cards.example_reading: せんせい に ちゅうい されて、 かれ は きゅう に たいど を かえた。
cards.example_meaning: After the teacher warned him, he suddenly changed his attitude.

cards.scene: 'Mitsuha' talks and moves like a rough boy, and her classmates can't believe it.
cards.context: な-adjective and noun: 乱暴な言葉 = rough language; 乱暴に扱う = to handle roughly. For speech, 言葉遣いが乱暴 is a common combination. 乱暴する can mean actual violence, so it's a strong word.
cards.example_sentence: 本を乱暴に扱わないでください。
cards.example_reading: ほん を らんぼう に あつかわないで ください。
cards.example_meaning: Please don't handle the books roughly.

cards.scene: The classroom buzzes because 'Mitsuha' is acting like a completely different girl.
cards.context: 騒ぐ = to be noisy or worked up (教室で騒ぐ), or to make a fuss about something. 騒がしい = noisy; 大騒ぎ (おおさわぎ) = an uproar.
cards.example_sentence: 図書館で騒いではいけません。
cards.example_reading: としょかん で さわいで は いけません。
cards.example_meaning: You mustn't make noise in the library.

cards.scene: Friends on both sides wonder whether 'Taki' and 'Mitsuha' have become different people overnight.
cards.context: 性格がいい / 明るい / 暗い = a good / cheerful / gloomy personality. 性格が変わる = to change as a person. 人柄 (ひとがら) is a warmer, more formal word.
cards.example_sentence: 姉と私は顔はそっくりだが、性格は正反対だ。
cards.example_reading: あね と わたし は かお は そっくり だ が、 せいかく は せいはんたい だ。
cards.example_meaning: My sister and I look exactly alike, but our personalities are complete opposites.

cards.scene: 三葉 wakes up in a Tokyo apartment where 瀧 lives with just his father.
cards.context: 父親 / 母親 are neutral words for someone's father / mother, common in narration. Your own father is 父 (ちち) in polite speech; someone else's is お父さん. 父親似 = takes after one's father.
cards.example_sentence: 彼は父親に似て、背が高い。
cards.example_reading: かれ は ちちおや に にて、 せ が たかい。
cards.example_meaning: He's tall, like his father.

cards.scene: Instead of an old house in the mountains, 三葉 wakes up in a city apartment.
cards.context: False friend: マンション is an ordinary apartment block (usually concrete, several floors), not a 'mansion'. アパート = a smaller, cheaper building, often two storeys. 十階 (じゅっかい) = the tenth floor.
cards.example_sentence: うちのマンションの十階からは、富士山が見える。
cards.example_reading: うち の マンション の じゅっかい から は、 ふじさん が みえる。
cards.example_meaning: You can see Mt Fuji from the tenth floor of our apartment building.

cards.scene: From the window and the streets, 三葉 takes in the Tokyo view she has only ever seen on screens.
cards.context: Irregular reading: 景色 = けしき. 景色がいい = there's a great view. 風景 (ふうけい) is similar but more 'the scene as a picture'; 夜景 (やけい) = a night view of city lights.
cards.example_sentence: 山の上から見た景色は、本当にきれいだった。
cards.example_reading: やま の うえ から みた けしき は、 ほんとう に きれい だった。
cards.example_meaning: The view from the top of the mountain was really beautiful.

cards.scene: Tokyo's busy streets: the city 三葉 has always dreamed about.
cards.context: Both 街 and 町 are read まち. 町 = a town as a place where people live (Itomori is a 町); 街 = busy streets with shops and lights. 街角 (まちかど) = a street corner.
cards.example_sentence: 夜の街は、昼間とは違う顔を見せる。
cards.example_reading: よる の まち は、 ひるま と は ちがう かお を みせる。
cards.example_meaning: At night, the city shows a different face from the daytime.

cards.scene: Tokyo's morning trains and stations are packed, which is a shock for a girl from a small town.
cards.context: Usually in the ている form: 電車が混んでいる = the train is crowded. Also written 込む. Opposite: 空いている (すいている) = not crowded. 混雑 (こんざつ) is the formal noun.
cards.example_sentence: 朝の電車はいつも混んでいて、座れない。
cards.example_reading: あさ の でんしゃ は いつも こんで いて、 すわれない。
cards.example_meaning: The morning train is always crowded, so I can't get a seat.

cards.scene: Fits 三葉's first Tokyo commute through a maze of train lines.
cards.context: 〜で…に乗り換える = to change to … at ~ (新宿で中央線に乗り換える). Noun: 乗り換え = a transfer. The hard Ch.4 word 乗り継ぐ means making connections on a long journey.
cards.example_sentence: 東京駅で新幹線に乗り換えてください。
cards.example_reading: とうきょうえき で しんかんせん に のりかえて ください。
cards.example_meaning: Please change to the bullet train at Tokyo Station.

cards.scene: Huge Tokyo crossings full of people, a world away from Itomori's quiet roads.
cards.context: 交 (cross) + 差 + 点 (point). 交差点を右に曲がる = to turn right at the intersection. 信号 (しんごう) = traffic light; 横断歩道 (おうだんほどう) = pedestrian crossing.
cards.example_sentence: 次の交差点を左に曲がると、駅があります。
cards.example_reading: つぎ の こうさてん を ひだり に まがる と、 えき が あります。
cards.example_meaning: Turn left at the next intersection and you'll find the station.

cards.scene: Just walking around Tokyo thrills 三葉 and moves her.
cards.context: 感動する = to be moved (by a film, a view, someone's kindness). 感動的 = moving. Compare 感心 (admiring someone's skill) and 感激 (かんげき, overjoyed, a stronger word).
cards.example_sentence: その映画を見て、とても感動した。
cards.example_reading: その えいが を みて、 とても かんどう した。
cards.example_meaning: I was really moved by that film.

cards.scene: 司 and 高木 can tell their friend isn't his usual self today.
cards.context: 普段は = normally; 普段の〜 = everyday ~ (普段の生活, 普段着 ふだんぎ = everyday clothes). いつも = always; 普段 = as a rule, in daily life.
cards.example_sentence: 普段はおとなしい彼が、今日は大きな声で笑っていた。
cards.example_reading: ふだん は おとなしい かれ が、 きょう は おおきな こえ で わらって いた。
cards.example_meaning: He's normally quiet, but today he was laughing loudly.

cards.scene: Every time 三葉 slips into girl-speech in front of 瀧's friends, she has to laugh it off.
cards.context: 笑ってごまかす = to laugh something off; 年をごまかす = to lie about your age; お金をごまかす = to cheat someone out of money. The kanji 誤魔化す is rarely used.
cards.example_sentence: 宿題を忘れたことを、笑ってごまかした。
cards.example_reading: しゅくだい を わすれた こと を、 わらって ごまかした。
cards.example_meaning: I laughed it off when I'd forgotten my homework.

cards.scene: Embarrassing moments on both sides leave faces burning red.
cards.context: 顔が真っ赤になる = to go bright red. 真っ + a colour makes it stronger: 真っ白 (まっしろ), 真っ黒 (まっくろ), 真っ青 (まっさお, pale with fear). Note the special reading まっか.
cards.example_sentence: みんなの前で名前を呼ばれて、顔が真っ赤になった。
cards.example_reading: みんな の まえ で なまえ を よばれて、 かお が まっか に なった。
cards.example_meaning: When my name was called in front of everyone, my face went bright red.

cards.scene: After school, 三葉 gets to visit a stylish Tokyo café, exactly what she dreamed of.
cards.context: な-adjective: おしゃれな店 = a stylish shop. Also a noun / する-verb: おしゃれする = to dress up. The kanji お洒落 is rare. The hard deck's 洗練 is the formal word for 'refined'.
cards.example_sentence: 駅の近くに、おしゃれなカフェができた。
cards.example_reading: えき の ちかく に、 おしゃれな カフェ が できた。
cards.example_meaning: A stylish café has opened near the station.

cards.scene: Ordering at the café, and later taking orders as a waiter.
cards.context: 注文する = to order. ご注文は? = What would you like? (a waiter's phrase). In casual speech people often say 頼む: コーヒーを頼む.
cards.example_sentence: ご注文はお決まりですか。
cards.example_reading: ごちゅうもん は おきまり です か。
cards.example_meaning: Are you ready to order?

cards.scene: Tokyo café prices are a surprise for a girl used to small-town costs.
cards.context: 値段が高い / 安い (not 大きい / 小さい). 値段を聞く = to ask the price. 値段 is the everyday word; 価格 (かかく) is formal and used on price tags.
cards.example_sentence: このケーキはおいしいけど、値段がちょっと高い。
cards.example_reading: この ケーキ は おいしい けど、 ねだん が ちょっと たかい。
cards.example_meaning: This cake is delicious, but it's a bit expensive.

cards.scene: 瀧 works part-time as a waiter at an Italian restaurant, and 三葉 has to cover his shift.
cards.context: Short for アルバイト (from the German Arbeit). バイトする = to work part-time; バイト先 = where you work part-time. パート is the usual word for adults' part-time work.
cards.example_sentence: 週に三回、駅前のパン屋でバイトしている。
cards.example_reading: しゅう に さんかい、 えきまえ の パンや で バイト して いる。
cards.example_meaning: I work part-time at the bakery in front of the station three times a week.

cards.scene: 奥寺先輩 is the older, much-admired co-worker at 瀧's restaurant.
cards.context: Anyone who started school or work before you. It's also used as a title: 奥寺先輩. Opposite: 後輩 (こうはい) = junior. 同期 (どうき) = someone who started at the same time.
cards.example_sentence: バイト先の先輩に、仕事を丁寧に教えてもらった。
cards.example_reading: バイトさき の せんぱい に、 しごと を ていねい に おしえて もらった。
cards.example_meaning: A senior co-worker at my part-time job taught me the work carefully.

cards.scene: 奥寺先輩 is the restaurant's beautiful, popular senior.
cards.context: Normally said of women. 美しい is the adjective 'beautiful'. イケメン (Ch.1) is the casual word for a handsome man.
cards.example_sentence: 彼女のお姉さんは、町で有名な美人だ。
cards.example_reading: かのじょ の おねえさん は、 まち で ゆうめいな びじん だ。
cards.example_meaning: Her older sister is a well-known beauty in town.

cards.scene: Restaurant customers, including one who causes serious trouble.
cards.context: Polite forms: お客さん (everyday), お客様 (staff speaking to customers). 客席 = seats for customers or an audience; 乗客 (じょうきゃく) = a passenger.
cards.example_sentence: 週末の店は、お客さんでいっぱいだった。
cards.example_reading: しゅうまつ の みせ は、 おきゃくさん で いっぱい だった。
cards.example_meaning: The shop was full of customers on the weekend.

cards.scene: Covering a waiter's shift she has never done before, 三葉 struggles to avoid mistakes.
cards.context: 失敗する = to fail, to mess up. ミスする is casual and used for small slips. Saying: 失敗は成功のもと = failure is the first step to success.
cards.example_sentence: 初めての仕事で、たくさん失敗した。
cards.example_reading: はじめて の しごと で、 たくさん しっぱい した。
cards.example_meaning: I made lots of mistakes at my first job.

cards.scene: Saying sorry to customers is part of the job, even in someone else's body.
cards.context: 〜に謝る = to apologize to someone. 謝罪 (しゃざい) is the formal noun. The same kanji is in 感謝 (かんしゃ, gratitude). Staff apologize with 申し訳ございません (very polite).
cards.example_sentence: 約束を忘れて、友だちに謝った。
cards.example_reading: やくそく を わすれて、 ともだち に あやまった。
cards.example_meaning: I forgot our plans, so I apologized to my friend.

cards.scene: A rude customer starts complaining and giving the staff a hard time.
cards.context: 文句を言う = to complain. 文句なし = perfect, no complaints. The hard deck's クレーム is a complaint made to a business; 文句 is everyday grumbling.
cards.example_sentence: 弟は、晩ご飯が遅いと文句を言っている。
cards.example_reading: おとうと は、 ばんごはん が おそい と もんく を いって いる。
cards.example_meaning: My little brother is complaining that dinner is late.

cards.scene: The troublesome customer makes things hard for everyone in the restaurant.
cards.context: 迷惑をかける = to cause someone trouble; 迷惑な客 = a nuisance customer; ご迷惑をおかけしました = sorry for the trouble (a set apology). 迷 is the same kanji as in 迷う.
cards.example_sentence: 夜遅くに大きな音を出すと、近所に迷惑だよ。
cards.example_reading: よる おそく に おおきな おと を だす と、 きんじょ に めいわく だ よ。
cards.example_meaning: Making loud noises late at night bothers the neighbours.

cards.scene: 奥寺先輩 is left with a torn skirt after the customer slashes it.
cards.context: Intransitive: something tears. Transitive 破る = to tear, and also to break a promise or rule (約束を破る). Use 破れる for cloth and paper; 切れる for things that snap or are cut.
cards.example_sentence: 転んだときに、ズボンのひざが破れた。
cards.example_reading: ころんだ とき に、 ズボン の ひざ が やぶれた。
cards.example_meaning: When I fell, the knee of my trousers ripped.

cards.scene: With a needle and thread, 三葉 in 瀧's body repairs 奥寺先輩's skirt.
cards.context: 針に糸を通す = to thread a needle. 時計の針 = the hands of a clock; 釣り針 (つりばり) = a fishing hook; 注射針 = a syringe needle.
cards.example_sentence: 細い針に糸を通すのは、なかなか難しい。
cards.example_reading: ほそい はり に いと を とおす の は、 なかなか むずかしい。
cards.example_meaning: Threading a fine needle is pretty difficult.

cards.scene: Instead of panicking, 'Taki' calmly fixes the ruined skirt.
cards.context: Intransitive pair: 直る = to get fixed. Also 'to correct': 間違いを直す. Vます + 直す = to redo: 書き直す, 言い直す. For curing an illness, use 治す (same reading).
cards.example_sentence: 父は、こわれた自転車を自分で直した。
cards.example_reading: ちち は、 こわれた じてんしゃ を じぶん で なおした。
cards.example_meaning: My father fixed the broken bicycle himself.

cards.scene: Nobody expected 'Taki' to be so good with a needle. It's a surprising side of him.
cards.context: な-adjective: 意外な一面 = an unexpected side of someone. 意外と / 意外に = surprisingly: 意外と簡単 = surprisingly easy. The opposite idea is 予想通り = just as expected.
cards.example_sentence: 怖そうな先生だったが、話してみると意外に優しかった。
cards.example_reading: こわそうな せんせい だった が、 はなして みる と いがい に やさしかった。
cards.example_meaning: The teacher looked scary, but when I talked to him, he was surprisingly kind.

cards.scene: Everyone is impressed by how neatly 'Taki' sews up the tear.
cards.context: 感心する = to admire someone's skill, effort or good behaviour (感動 = to be emotionally moved). Don't confuse it with 関心 (かんしん, interest): 政治に関心がある.
cards.example_sentence: 弟が毎朝早く起きて勉強しているので、感心した。
cards.example_reading: おとうと が まいあさ はやく おきて べんきょう して いる ので、 かんしん した。
cards.example_meaning: I was impressed that my little brother gets up early every morning to study.

cards.scene: 奥寺先輩 praises 'Taki' for his surprising skill.
cards.context: 人を褒める; passive 褒められる = to be praised. Often written in kana: ほめる. Opposite: 叱る (しかる) = to scold.
cards.example_sentence: テストでいい点を取って、先生に褒められた。
cards.example_reading: テスト で いい てん を とって、 せんせい に ほめられた。
cards.example_meaning: I got a good score on the test, and the teacher praised me.

cards.scene: 奥寺先輩 thanks 'Taki' for getting her out of a bad situation.
cards.context: お礼を言う = to say thank you; お礼をする = to give something back as thanks. The kanji 礼 is also in 失礼 (しつれい) and 礼儀 (れいぎ, manners).
cards.example_sentence: 手伝ってくれたお礼に、ケーキを買ってきた。
cards.example_reading: てつだって くれた おれい に、 ケーキ を かって きた。
cards.example_meaning: I bought a cake to thank you for your help.

cards.scene: Back in their own bodies, both check their phones and find things they never wrote.
cards.context: Short for 携帯電話. スマホ (smartphone) is now just as common. 携帯する = to carry (formal); 携帯用 = portable, for carrying.
cards.example_sentence: 携帯を家に忘れて、一日中不便だった。
cards.example_reading: けいたい を いえ に わすれて、 いちにちじゅう ふべん だった。
cards.example_meaning: I left my phone at home and it was a pain all day.

cards.scene: Words they don't remember typing are right there on the phone screen.
cards.context: 画 (picture) + 面 (surface). スマホの画面 / テレビの画面. 画面が割れる = the screen cracks; 待ち受け画面 = home-screen picture.
cards.example_sentence: スマホの画面が割れてしまった。
cards.example_reading: スマホ の がめん が われて しまった。
cards.example_meaning: My smartphone screen got cracked.

cards.scene: Notes and diary entries left behind by the other person are the first clues.
cards.context: Transitive; the intransitive pair is 残る = to remain. メモを残す = to leave a note; ご飯を残す = to leave food uneaten; 伝言を残す = to leave a message.
cards.example_sentence: 母は「先に寝ます」とメモを残して、寝てしまった。
cards.example_reading: はは は 「さき に ねます」 と メモ を のこして、 ねて しまった。
cards.example_meaning: My mother left a note saying 'Going to bed first' and went to sleep.

cards.scene: Each of them is sure they never wrote those entries, yet there they are on the phone.
cards.context: 確かに = for sure; also used to agree: 確かにそうだね = you've got a point. Without に, 確か means 'if I remember right': 確か三時だった. 確かめる (to check) uses the same kanji.
cards.example_sentence: 確かに私の字だが、書いた覚えがない。
cards.example_reading: たしか に わたし の じ だ が、 かいた おぼえ が ない。
cards.example_meaning: It's definitely my handwriting, but I don't remember writing it.

cards.scene: Someone has been doing whatever they like with your body, your friends and your day, without asking.
cards.context: 勝手に使わないで = don't use it without asking. 勝手な人 / 自分勝手 = a selfish person. It can also mean 'by itself': ドアが勝手に開いた = the door opened on its own.
cards.example_sentence: 人の日記を勝手に読まないで!
cards.example_reading: ひと の にっき を かって に よまないで!
cards.example_meaning: Don't read my diary without asking!

cards.scene: The scary thought that someone else, a total stranger, was living in your body.
cards.context: 他人 = anyone who isn't you, often with an 'outsider' feel: 赤の他人 = a complete stranger; 他人のふり = acting as if you don't know someone. Compare 別人 (Ch.3) = a different person from before.
cards.example_sentence: 他人の意見ばかり気にしていたら、何も決められない。
cards.example_reading: たにん の いけん ばかり き に して いたら、 なにも きめられない。
cards.example_meaning: If you only worry about other people's opinions, you can't decide anything.

cards.scene: Bit by bit, both of them notice the clues and realise what is happening.
cards.context: 〜に気がつく = to notice ~ (with に). 気づく is a shorter form that is common in writing. 気がつくと = before I knew it. It also means 'to come round' after fainting.
cards.example_sentence: 電車を降りてから、かさを忘れたことに気がついた。
cards.example_reading: でんしゃ を おりて から、 かさ を わすれた こと に き が ついた。
cards.example_meaning: After getting off the train, I realised I'd left my umbrella behind.

cards.scene: 'Could it be…?' The suspicion grows that the dream is no dream at all.
cards.context: Introduces a guess you half believe: もしかして〜? = could it be ~? or 'by any chance': もしかして田中さんですか. もしかしたら = maybe (just a possibility). For stronger disbelief, use まさか.
cards.example_sentence: もしかして、あの人は昨日駅で会った人じゃない?
cards.example_reading: もしかして、 あの ひと は きのう えき で あった ひと じゃない?
cards.example_meaning: Could that be the person we met at the station yesterday?

cards.scene: Swapping bodies with a stranger? At first, neither of them can believe it.
cards.context: 〜を信じる. 信じられない = I can't believe it / unbelievable. 信じ込む = to firmly believe (often wrongly). 信用 (しんよう) = trust.
cards.example_sentence: 宝くじが当たったなんて、まだ信じられない。
cards.example_reading: たからくじ が あたった なんて、 まだ しんじられない。
cards.example_meaning: I still can't believe I won the lottery.

cards.scene: Once the clues pile up: so it really did happen after all.
cards.context: Casual form of やはり, which is more written or formal. Means 'just as I thought' or 'after all (I changed my mind)': やっぱりやめる = on second thought, I won't. Even more casual: やっぱ.
cards.example_sentence: 迷ったけど、やっぱり赤いほうを買うことにした。
cards.example_reading: まよった けど、 やっぱり あかい ほう を かう こと に した。
cards.example_meaning: I couldn't decide, but in the end I went with the red one.
